sector: Industrial IoT / Commercial Refrigeration Hardware & SaaS
overview: AoFrio Limited (formerly Wellington Drive Technologies, renamed September 2022) is a New Zealand-headquartered, NZX-listed hardware-enabled SaaS company that designs and manufactures energy-efficient electronically commutated (EC) motors and fans, and IoT-enabled smart controllers/cloud connectivity (SCS Connect, SCS 800, AoFrio iQ) for commercial refrigeration in the food and beverage industry, principally bottle coolers used by Coca-Cola system bottlers, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo and other global beverage brands. The company reports two segments, Motors and IoT, sells globally with heavy revenue concentration in the Americas (LATAM plus USA), and is pursuing diversification into Food Retail and Chilled/Frozen Food adjacent markets while transitioning from a hardware-led business toward a hardware-enabled, AI-powered SaaS model.

business_model.summary: Revenue splits between hardware sales of EC motors/fans (commoditized, lower margin, largely transactional) and IoT hardware plus recurring multi-year cloud data/software connection fees (higher margin, increasingly recurring). FY25 (year ended 31-Dec-2025) revenue was NZ$83.2m (+4.4% YoY): IoT NZ$47.1m (+8.9%, 42.5% gross margin) and Motors NZ$36.1m (flat, 17.7% gross margin). However, 1H26 (six months to 30-Jun-2026) revenue fell sharply to $33.8m (down 21.5% YoY) as Motors revenue collapsed to $10.6m (down 50.5%, -$10.8m) following the loss of AoFrio's largest US motor customer to tariff-driven onshoring; IoT revenue held up, growing 6.8% to $23.2m and now represents the clear majority of group revenue. Gross margin improved to 34.9% in 1H26 (from 29.6% in 1H25) purely on mix-shift toward higher-margin IoT, even as absolute revenue and EBITDA quality (aided by a one-off $1.2m RDTI tax credit in the $0.9m 1H26 EBITDA) softened. Recurring SaaS/data revenue was only 3.8% of FY25 revenue recognized ($3.2m) against a long-term target of 50%, with $17.8m of contract liability (deferred revenue) on the balance sheet to be recognized over 1-10 year contracts as the installed base of connected devices (3.2m at FY25 year-end, +22% YoY) converts to recognized revenue.

revenue_streams.name: Motors and Fans
revenue_streams.trend: declining sharply (1H26 -50.5% YoY on lost US customer)

revenue_streams.name: Recurring cloud/SaaS revenue (subset of IoT, recognized)

business_model.customer_type: B2B - enterprise, historically concentrated among global beverage bottlers/brands (Coca-Cola system bottlers, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo), OEMs, and USA appliance/water-heater manufacturers; FY25 saw four customers each individually >=10% of revenue together account for 49% of Group revenue ($40.5m of $83.2m), all within the Americas segment (up from two customers/27% in FY24); the single largest USA motor customer has now been lost in 2026 (onshoring supply to avoid tariffs), crystallizing the concentration risk flagged in FY25
business_model.geographic_mix: Americas ~85% (LATAM plus USA) in FY25, APAC 8.3%, EMEA 7.0%; North America previously a growth driver via ECR2 motors into water heaters/supermarket display units and early SCS IoT launch, now the source of the 2026 Motors downturn; South America (core CDE/LATAM base) revenue declined 12.5% YoY in FY25 on reduced demand

main_competitors: Generic/local EC motor and fan manufacturers (especially in EMEA on price)
In-house/legacy telemetry and asset-tracking vendors for cooler fleets
Traditional AC-motor incumbents being displaced by EC technology
competitive_position.market_position: Long-established, high-share incumbent supplier of EC motors/fans and connected controllers to the global cold drink equipment (CDE)/bottle cooler market, particularly strong in LATAM; a much smaller, earlier-stage challenger in IoT-enabled fleet SaaS platforms versus larger industrial IoT and cold-chain software players

moat_factors.description: SCS/Monitor/Click devices installed on coolers create a base of ~3.2m connected devices and long-dated (1-10 year) data contracts, generating switching costs once fleets are connected and integrated into customer operations

Decades-long relationships with global beverage brands and bottlers (Coca-Cola system, Heineken, Nestle, PepsiCo) and high customer NPS (+62, up 9pts in FY25) support renewal and cross-sell, though this coexists with severe customer concentration risk that has now materialized (loss of largest US motor customer in 2026)

ECR2 motor technology delivers validated energy savings (up to 68% in bundled configurations) that align with customer ESG targets and evolving efficiency regulations (e.g., US DOE water heater standards), supporting product pull-through

Growing connected fleet (3.2m devices, app utilisation up 31% in FY25) improves AoFrio iQ's fleet insights and product value, but the platform only reached commercial launch in mid-2026 (33 global trials underway, first purchase orders anticipated 2H26) and remains unproven at scale

Micro-cap scale (market cap roughly NZ$25-45m depending on share price) limits R&D budget, negotiating leverage and resilience versus larger diversified industrial competitors; balance sheet fragility constrains ability to fund the more ambitious growth path without dilutive equity raises

weaknesses: Motors segment is a commoditized, price-competitive, low-margin (17.7% FY25) business exposed to aggressive competitor pricing (notably in EMEA) and tariff-driven customer reshoring; this materialized in 1H26 with a 50.5% Motors revenue collapse

Customer concentration risk crystallized: the single largest USA motor customer sourced elsewhere in 2026 due to tariffs, directly causing the group revenue decline; four customers = 49% of FY25 revenue, all in the Americas

Recurring/SaaS revenue still tiny (3.8% of FY25 revenue) relative to the 50% long-term target; AoFrio iQ and SCS 800 only reached commercial launch in mid-2026 and are still ramping (purchase orders not yet flowing at scale)

Fragile balance sheet: net debt rose to $8.2m (from $2.5m) and cash fell to $1.3m at FY25 year-end (then $1.4m at 1Q26), funded partly via extended supplier payment terms and an enlarged trade finance facility; the 2026 capital raise (placement + rights issue) has so far only delivered $8.9m of the $15m targeted for the accelerated growth path

growth_drivers: Commercial launch of SCS 800 cellular-connected controller and AoFrio iQ SaaS platform both completed in mid-2026, with 33 global customer trials underway and first purchase orders anticipated in 2H26, targeting a combined ~700,000-unit/year US/Europe/Canada cellular controller TAM

Food Retail vertical achieved commercial go-live in 2026 with a first order secured from a Latin American supermarket chain following a successful trial, building on the FY25 NZ convenience-store (115 sites) and Chilled/Frozen Food (pet food, ~3,500 freezers) wins

New fan pack sizes (7", 8", 9", 10") and new motor applications (e.g., ECR2 into beverage-dispenser agitators) intended to protect/expand Motors margin and unit volumes even as the largest US customer is lost

Two-path FY26-FY30 growth strategy presented at December 2025 Investor Day: self-funded path targeting ~10% revenue CAGR to ~$140m/EBITDA $14m by FY30, versus an externally-capitalized 'aspirational' path targeting >3x revenue to $300m and EBITDA of $50m by FY30; the Board's preferred (aspirational) path is now partly funded via the May-June 2026 placement/rights issue ($8.9m raised of $15m target), with capital deployment beginning 2H26
Secular tailwind from cold-chain energy efficiency, refrigerant/ESG regulation, and increasing enterprise appetite for connected/AI-driven asset management across cooler fleets

Management (Chair John Scott) has publicly framed the 2026 Motors downturn as a one-off 'blip' with 2Q26 revenue expected broadly in line with 2Q25 and recovery expected in subsequent quarters, implying management still sees the underlying IoT/CDE growth trajectory intact

business.risk: Customer concentration crystallizing into realized losses
business.description: AoFrio's single largest USA motor customer has now been lost (onshoring supply to avoid tariffs), directly driving the 50.5% Motors revenue decline and 21.5% total revenue decline in 1H26; FY25 saw four customers at 49% of revenue, up from two customers/27% in FY24, underscoring a worsening concentration trend that has now materially hit results

Motors and Fans is a lower-margin (17.7% FY25), price-competitive category facing aggressive competitor pricing (EMEA revenue fell 8.8% YoY in FY25) and is now also structurally shrinking in the Americas post the largest customer's exit

business.risk: Execution risk on new product/SaaS launches
business.description: Growth thesis depends heavily on SCS 800 and AoFrio iQ converting from commercial launch (mid-2026) and 33 active trials into meaningful purchase orders; management itself flagged in the 1H26 result that 'the improvement in full-year revenue now appears unlikely' for FY26

business.risk: Product obsolescence / long sales and qualification cycles
business.description: OEM/bottler capital purchase cycles are multi-year; new hardware must pass customer qualification programmes, slowing revenue realization from new launches

financial.risk: Rising net debt and thin liquidity
financial.description: Net debt increased from $2.5m to $8.2m and cash fell to $1.3m at 31-Dec-2025 (further to $1.4m by 1Q26); working capital pressure from longer customer payment terms, higher inventory and increased reliance on extended supplier payment terms (contract manufacturer East West) and an enlarged trade finance facility

Company has posted statutory net losses in recent years (FY25 loss $2.1m, FY24 loss $1.9m); annual and interim reports include going-concern assessments dependent on Board-approved budget assumptions and continued bank trade facility support; the FY26 revenue shortfall increases pressure on these assumptions

financial.risk: Shareholder dilution, partially executed but incomplete
financial.description: May 2026 placement (65.1m shares at NZ$0.07 to Wairahi Investments, $4.6m) plus a 1-for-7 renounceable rights issue at the same $0.07 price raised $8.9m combined against a $15m target for the accelerated growth path; the shortfall implies either scaled-back growth ambitions or a further dilutive raise; share count has grown materially from ~431.9m (FY24) toward 500m+ post-raise

Functional currency is USD but presentation currency is NZD; FY26 guidance assumptions were based on a 0.606 NZD/USD rate and management has flagged NZD strengthening as an adverse headwind to reported revenue and profit

regulatory.description: April 2025 US reciprocal tariffs have now materially cost AoFrio its largest USA motor customer (previously ~US$5.6m FY25 revenue), driving the 50.5% 1H26 Motors revenue decline; this is the single biggest realized risk event in the company's recent history and there is no indication of resolution or replacement business as of mid-2026
Reliance on a Vietnam-based contract manufacturer (East West) for motor production creates ongoing exposure to further shifts in US trade policy toward Vietnam-origin goods
Changing regulatory standards (e.g., US DOE water heater efficiency standards) can be a tailwind (driving ECR2 motor adoption) but also a compliance cost and uncertainty factor

macro.description: Broader macroeconomic headwinds from US tariff policy caused subdued customer capital spending through H1-2025 and has now directly cost the company its largest customer in 2026, with management declining to provide confident full-year guidance
Bottler/OEM capital purchase cycles are discretionary and can be deferred in a weaker macro environment, directly affecting AoFrio's hardware sell-through
Rising bank borrowings and trade finance usage make the company sensitive to interest rate levels; finance costs increased $0.3m in FY25 due to increased borrowings and extended payment terms

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Commercial refrigeration / cold drink equipment is a mature, essential replacement-and-growth market with a structural shift toward energy-efficient EC motor technology and IoT-enabled fleet management, reinforced by ESG/carbon-reduction targets among major beverage brands (refrigeration is ~35% of a cold drink's carbon footprint per company disclosure) and rising enterprise demand for connected asset management and AI-driven insights; however, the Motors sub-segment is now visibly exposed to US trade policy shocks that can remove large customers abruptly
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - revenue tied to customer capital expenditure cycles (bottler/OEM cooler fleet renewal and expansion) which can be deferred in weaker macro conditions or amid trade-policy uncertainty, as evidenced by the 1H26 downturn triggered by tariff-driven customer reshoring
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - increasing use of bank trade finance and borrowings to fund working capital and growth investment means finance costs rise with base rates and facility utilization
key_input_costs: Electronic components and motor/fan raw materials (contract-manufactured in Vietnam)
Ocean freight/shipping (longer shipping times cited as a working capital driver)
Cloud/software engineering and R&D talent costs

recent_developments.event: FY2025 annual results released: record revenue of NZ$83.2m (+4.4%), EBITDA $3.5m (+$1.0m), gross margin 31.7% (+2.6pp), but revenue came in below the September 2025 updated guidance of ~$86m due to Q4-25 US tariff-driven motor demand weakness

Investor Day: management presented two FY26-FY30 growth paths - self-funded (~10% revenue CAGR to ~$140m/EBITDA $14m by FY30) versus an externally capitalized 'aspirational' path (>3x revenue to $300m, EBITDA $50m by FY30); several shareholders indicated support for the higher-growth path
Placement of 65,134,806 shares to Wairahi Investments Limited at NZ$0.07/share raising NZ$4.559m, the first stage of securing growth capital for the accelerated ('aspirational') strategy

Announced and executed a 1-for-7 pro-rata renounceable rights issue at NZ$0.07/share (opened 5 June, closed 18 June 2026); combined placement plus rights issue raised $8.9m against a $15m target for the accelerated growth path

1Q26 trading update: revenue $17.2m, down 28.1% YoY, as Motor revenue fell 52.9% to $5.7m following the loss of the largest US motor customer to tariff-driven onshoring; EBITDA -$0.4m (vs +$1.5m 1Q25); cash $1.4m; Chair John Scott described it as the company's first quarterly 'blip' after a run of predictable results, expecting recovery in subsequent quarters

Commercial launch of SCS 800 cellular controller and AoFrio iQ SaaS platform completed; 33 global customer trials underway with first purchase orders anticipated in 2H26; Food Retail vertical achieved commercial go-live with a first order from a Latin American supermarket chain

1H26 revenue $33.8m, down 21.5% YoY, entirely attributable to the 50.5% (-$10.8m) Motors revenue decline; IoT revenue grew 6.8% to $23.2m and is now the majority of group revenue; gross margin improved to 34.9% (from 29.6%) on mix shift; EBITDA $0.9m (aided by a $1.2m one-off 2025 RDTI tax credit); management stated 'the improvement in full-year revenue now appears unlikely' for FY26, with EBITDA expected 'broadly consistent with 2025' and IoT revenue expected above 2025 levels

items.target: Full-year revenue improvement over FY25 ($83.2m) now considered unlikely
items.notes: At FY25 results (Feb-2026) management expected FY26 revenue to exceed FY25 across all segments; by the 1H26 interim result (Aug-2026) this was walked back given the Motors collapse from the lost largest US customer and uncertain trading environment
IoT revenue specifically still expected to be above FY2025 levels, i.e. the shortfall is concentrated in Motors
Guided at the 1Q26 trading update following the Q1 'blip'; actual 1H26 result implies 2Q26 performance roughly matched this expectation given 1H26 total of $33.8m

items.target: $15m target for the accelerated ('aspirational') growth path; $8.9m raised to date via placement + rights issue
items.notes: Company stated it will adjust its plan to align with the capital actually raised and will commence deploying the $8.9m in 2H26 to accelerate CDE growth; implies either a scaled-down version of the aspirational path or a further capital raise to close the gap to $15m

items.target: 20% per annum revenue growth with 50% of revenue recurring (longer-term strategic goal) — refined at Dec-2025 Investor Day into two explicit paths: ~10% CAGR self-funded to $140m FY30 revenue/$14m EBITDA, or an externally funded 'aspirational' path targeting $300m FY30 revenue/$50m EBITDA
items.vs_prior: maintained as strategic framework, though FY26 starting point is now weaker than assumed in December 2025
items.notes: The FY26 Motors shortfall and partial capital raise both create execution risk against these FY30 targets

items.target: Commercial launch completed mid-2026; 33 global trials underway; first purchase orders anticipated 2H26
items.notes: This is now the key swing factor for whether IoT growth can offset the structural Motors decline

guidance.management_commentary: Chair John Scott described 1Q26 as the company's first quarterly 'blip' after a run of predictable, reliable results, attributing it to the anticipated but still material loss of the largest US motor customer to tariffs, and expressed confidence in recovery in subsequent quarters. By the 1H26 interim result, management tempered this to say full-year revenue improvement over FY25 'now appears unlikely,' while reiterating EBITDA should be broadly consistent with FY25 and that IoT revenue specifically is expected to exceed FY25 levels — i.e., management is framing the shortfall as isolated to the lower-margin, structurally challenged Motors segment rather than a failure of the core IoT/SaaS growth strategy. Management also confirmed the $8.9m capital raised (against a $15m target) will begin to be deployed in 2H26 to accelerate CDE growth.

bull_case: IoT segment continues to grow through the downturn (+6.8% in 1H26 to $23.2m, +8.9% in FY25) and now represents the clear majority of revenue at improving gross margins (34.9% blended 1H26, 42.5% IoT-specific in FY25), validating the hardware-to-SaaS transition even as Motors struggles

SCS 800 cellular controller and AoFrio iQ SaaS platform both reached commercial launch in mid-2026 with 33 active global trials and first purchase orders expected 2H26, opening a combined ~700,000-unit US/Europe TAM and a path toward the long-stated 50% recurring-revenue target (still only 3.8% today, so a small starting base with a long theoretical runway)

Diversification into Food Retail (commercial go-live and first Latin American supermarket order in 2026) and Chilled/Frozen Food verticals reduces long-term dependence on the volatile CDE/bottle cooler and Motors business

Deep, multi-decade OEM/bottler relationships and high customer satisfaction (NPS +62 in FY25) plus proven energy-efficiency technology (up to 68% validated energy savings) support a durable secular tailwind independent of the near-term Motors setback

Management has begun deploying freshly raised growth capital ($8.9m) in 2H26 specifically to accelerate CDE/IoT growth, and has publicly framed the FY26 shortfall as an isolated, anticipated Motors 'blip' rather than a broader strategic failure
bear_case: The single largest customer-concentration risk flagged in FY25 has now fully crystallized: loss of the largest US motor customer drove a 50.5% Motors revenue collapse and a 21.5% total revenue decline in 1H26, with management now admitting full-year revenue improvement over FY25 'now appears unlikely' — guidance has been walked back within a single half-year

Balance sheet remains fragile: net debt roughly tripled to $8.2m and cash fell to $1.3m-$1.4m through FY25 and into 2026, funded via extended supplier terms and trade finance; the 2026 capital raise fell well short of its $15m target (only $8.9m raised), suggesting further dilution may be needed to fund the 'aspirational' growth path

Meaningful shareholder dilution already executed (May-June 2026 placement plus 1-for-7 rights issue at NZ$0.07/share, both below prior trading levels), with the funding shortfall implying more dilution risk ahead if management still wants to pursue the higher-growth path

Motors segment remains structurally challenged - commoditized, margin-thin (17.7% FY25 gross margin), losing share to competitor pricing in EMEA, and now missing its largest US customer entirely - while core recurring-SaaS revenue is still just 3.8% of total revenue versus a 50% aspiration that remains years away and unproven at commercial scale (SCS 800/AoFrio iQ only just launched)

Track record of guidance misses and revisions (FY25 revenue missed the revised $86m guide; FY26 guidance was withdrawn, then re-set, then effectively lowered again by August 2026) underscores low earnings visibility for a thinly capitalized micro-cap exposed to unpredictable US trade policy
